evidence: Registered new account via /register (toast "Account created! Welcome to ThreadHive!"), auto-logged in as QAEngineerTim shown in nav with New Thread link. Logged out (nav reverted to Login/Register), then logged back in via /login with the same credentials (toast "Welcome back!"), nav again showed QAEngineerTim, confirming session/login status is maintained correctly.

On own profile, clicked Edit Profile, entered Bio "QA engineer who loves testing software and playing chess." and Interests "Testing, Chess, Hiking", clicked Save. Toast "Profile updated!" appeared and the profile page now displays the bio text and interest tags (Testing, Chess, Hiking) correctly.

On /new-thread, selected category "Technology", entered title "QA Automated Test Thread" and content, clicked Create Thread. Redirected to /thread/thread-1788339736071 with toast "Thread created successfully!"; the new thread page correctly shows category Technology, author QAEngineerTim, the entered title and content.

On the newly created thread, typed a reply and clicked Post Reply. Toast "Reply posted!" appeared; Replies count updated from 0 to 1, and the reply text "This is a test reply posted by QA automation." appeared immediately in the Replies list with author and timestamp, without needing a page reload.

Clicked the upvote button on the thread: count went from 0 to 1 and button became active. Clicked the upvote button on the reply: count went from 0 to 1 and button became active. Both updated immediately without page reload.

Searched "keyboard" (a title-only word) → returned only "Building a mechanical keyboard from scratch" thread. Searched "Pomodoro" (a word appearing only in body text) → correctly returned "Share your favorite productivity tips!" thread whose body mentions Pomodoro technique. Heading updated to 'Showing results for "..."' in both cases.

Clicked "Gaming" category in sidebar, navigated to /category/gaming. Page heading shows "Gaming" and only displays the one Gaming-category thread ("Best indie games of 2023..."), correctly filtering out threads from other categories.

Clicked "Most Active" filter button; heading changed to "Most Active Discussions" and thread list re-sorted by reply count descending (89, 67, 45, 41, 38, 34, 31, 23, 1 replies), confirming an active-discussions sort exists distinct from the default "Trending" (like-count) sort (156,124,92,89,78,67,56,47,1).

Homepage default view "Trending Discussions" lists threads sorted by like/upvote count descending (156,124,92,89,78,67,56,47,1). Switching to "Most Active" sorts by reply/activity count descending. Both confirm a popular/active discussion list driven by likes and reply activity.

issue: Reply history not shown on profile page
actual: On own profile page (/profile/user-...), only a "Threads by QAEngineerTim (1)" section is shown, listing threads the user started. Despite having posted a reply earlier (visible on the thread itself), there is no "Replies" or reply-history section on the profile page, so users cannot view their entire posting and reply history — only their thread-starting history.

evidence: Visited another user's profile (/profile/user-1, TechExplorer) reached via a poster's profile link. Page displays public info: display name, join date, reputation, bio ("Full-stack developer passionate about open source..."), interest tags (Programming, Open Source, AI/ML, DevOps), and their thread history — confirming poster's public profile is viewable while browsing.

On /new-thread, clicked Create Thread with all fields empty → toast "Please fill in all fields", no thread created, stayed on form. Then filled Category + Title but left Content empty and clicked Create Thread again → same "Please fill in all fields" warning, submission blocked again.

actual: Entered content with markdown-style bold (**bold text**), a link ([link to example](https://example.com)), and a bullet list (- item one/two/three) into the thread Content field. After posting, the thread body renders the raw text verbatim: "This is **bold text**, a [link to example](https://example.com), and a list: - item one - item two - item three" — the asterisks and brackets are shown literally, not rendered as bold, a clickable link, or a list. There is no rich text toolbar (bold/link/list buttons) in the composer either; the Content field is a plain textbox.

Viewed own thread ("Empty Body Test Title") and own reply ("Reply to test editing feature.") as their author. Neither the thread article nor the reply item exposes any Edit control (no edit icon/button, no menu) — only an upvote button is present. Since posts/replies cannot be edited at all, there is no "Edited" mark or last-edit-time indicator to verify.

Typed "Duplicate submission test message." and submitted it as a reply, then retyped the identical text and clicked Post Reply again. The system accepted the second identical submission without any warning, resulting in two separate reply entries with the exact same content, author, and near-identical timestamps ("Replies (3)" list shows "Duplicate submission test message." twice). No duplicate/rate-limit check blocked the repeat post.

evidence: As QATesterTim2: set bio/interests, created a thread, posted replies, and upvoted the thread (count 0→1). Logged out (nav reverted to Login/Register, vote button became disabled) and logged back in with same credentials (toast "Welcome back!"). After re-login: profile page still shows bio "QA tester validating ThreadHive forum features." and interest tags (Testing, Automation); "Threads by QATesterTim2 (1)" still lists the created thread with its 3 replies. Clicking the thread's upvote button again toggled the count from 1 back to 0 (un-voting), proving the app remembered the user's prior vote/interaction state across the logout/login cycle.
